author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Downpours left some Massachusetts roads impassable over the weekend, with flooding reported in Fall River, New Bedford, Vineyard Haven, Plymouth and Wareham, Boston 25 News reported. The rain arrived as a National Weather Service flash-flood warning covered parts of the region.

Forecasters said localized rainfall totals could reach about four inches. The hardest-hit roads included low-lying routes and streets where water collected faster than drainage systems could clear it. Drivers were urged to avoid flooded roadways, where depth and pavement damage can be difficult to judge from a vehicle.

The heaviest rain was expected to taper by late Sunday, followed by a cooler and drier stretch during the workweek. Even after the main system moved out, officials warned that standing water and cleanup could continue to affect travel in communities that saw the most intense rain.
Residents should continue to treat flooded streets as dangerous even when water appears shallow, since currents and hidden hazards can affect vehicles and pedestrians.
dek: Heavy rain flooded roads in several Massachusetts communities, with the National Weather Service warning of localized totals of up to four inches.
headline: Flooding leaves Massachusetts roads impassable after weekend downpours
